label: deepseek-v4-pro-novita
_role: ENDPOINT variable. Same model and same prompt as the 2026-08-20 baseline, served by a different endpoint at a DECLARED fp8 quantization. The baseline ran on azure/us, which reports quantization 'unknown', so that leg could not separate model behaviour from serving stack. This leg closes that gap.
_cost_basis: NOT REPRODUCIBLE, and not billed. `core/pricing.py` is keyed on (provider, model) and cannot express a per-endpoint price, so price_for("openrouter", "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro") returns the azure/us row ($1.91 / $3.83 as of 2026-08-20) no matter what provider_order pins here. The cost this leg recorded ($0.24179236 on its one metered book; the other is unmetered and null) was therefore computed at the azure/us rate, NOT at the 1.44 / 2.88 novita rate above; the same metered counts at this pin's own rate come to about $0.182. A rerun reproduces the azure-priced figure, not the true novita spend. The recorded run data is preserved as evidence and must not be recomputed in place; see section 5.3 "Cost of this comparison" in docs/planning/deepseek-v4-pro-live-fill-plan-2026-08-20.md.

label: anthropic-sonnet-5
_role: MODEL variable, and the decisive one. If this leg honours the per-node words= directive where DeepSeek delivered 39-53 percent, then the shortfall is a MODEL property and the remedy is model selection, not a new gate rule. If it under-delivers too, the shortfall is a PROMPT property and UW-C307's fill-rate gate is the right fix. vendors.json calls this the checkpoint the pipeline actually runs.
_endpoint_verified: 2026-08-20, 200, served by Amazon Bedrock. First-party anthropic returns 404 under this account's data policy, same as vendors.json records.
